recommendation.label: Recommended with conditions
recommendation.headline: Strong location and ample space for a 40-seat restaurant — but HVAC/ventilation and kitchen infrastructure must be verified before signing.
recommendation.explanation:
This 5,212 sq ft commercial building sits in one of downtown Houston's densest food-and-beverage clusters, with heavy weekday office demand, rail access and no parking minimum (Downtown market-based parking area). Houston has no zoning, so the use is not restricted by a zoning district — but deed restrictions and any lease use clause still need checking.

The main uncertainty is mechanical: Vexcel detected no rooftop AC units. That does not mean the building lacks HVAC, but a restaurant needs substantial make-up air and a kitchen exhaust hood, so an on-site mechanical inspection is the deciding next step. The space is roughly twice what 40 seats need, which raises rent but leaves room for growth or a smaller sublease.

metrics.name: Kitchen ventilation & HVAC readiness
metrics.why_it_matters: Commercial kitchens need a Type I exhaust hood and make-up air; retrofitting rooftop equipment is one of the largest restaurant fit-out costs.
metrics.rationale: Vexcel detected 0 rooftop AC units. Equipment may be ground-mounted or interior, so HVAC capacity cannot be concluded from imagery.
assumptions: Flat membrane roof can structurally support a hood fan curb (unverified)

metrics.name: Space fit for 40 seats
metrics.why_it_matters: Too little space caps seating; too much raises rent and utilities.
metrics.rationale: Needs ~1,800–2,900 sq ft; footprint is 5,212 sq ft. Fits comfortably, with room for a larger kitchen or private dining.
assumptions: Single storey usable; interior layout unknown (no Matterport)

metrics.name: Roof & building condition

metrics.rationale: Roof condition 4.0/5 (Good), minor water pooling on 4.2% of the roof, no structural damage.
